text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: multiple GPU host reboots observed in us-central-1, cluster=redwood-serving-prod, spike started ~15:12 UTC. Auto-alert threshold tripped (reboots > 5 in 10m).
carla_oncall: I'm on it. setting channel to #incidents and will collect timeline. will shadow traffic to fallback region (us-east).
carla_oncall: quick mitigation - enabling model-fallback routing for low-latency tier, reducing batch_size to 1 for affected routes.
dave_sre: ack. can someone paste the host ids and recent kernel logs? I'll pull node telemetry and start a timeline.
frank_runtime: grabbing logs now. initial grep shows repeated AER PCIe errors + GPU ECC counts increasing on hosts gpu-az3-07 & gpu-az3-09. snippet:```
[ 3456.123456] pcieport 0000:00:1c.0: AER: Multiple Uncorrected (Non-Fatal) error messages
[ 3456.123789] nvidia: GPU 0: ECC single-bit error, incremented
[ 3457.233000] Kernel panic - not syncing: GPU driver oops
```
frank_runtime: also seeing nvlink timeouts on those nodes. attaching full syslog to the incident runbook: https://internal.redwood/incident/2112345678/logs
maya_platform: noisy-neighbor hypothesis is plausible — these hosts were scheduled with a new batch job (internal-embeddings) last night. that job requested 4 GPUs and was set to allow preemption. cc @carla_oncall
olivia_support: PSA: we've surface-level customer impact for 3 small customers — latency spikes and a few 5xx in the last 20m. CS is drafting outreach.
carla_oncall: thanks. frank, any memory ECC counts delta per GPU?
frank_runtime: per-gpu ECC single-bit counts: gpu-az3-07:[2,1,0,0] -> after spike [120,4,0,0]; gpu-az3-09:[0,0,0,0] -> [98,0,0,0]. pattern: a single slot in each host spiking.
dave_sre: that smells like either a failing DIMM on the host or PCIe fabric corruption. can we trigger a graceful drain and reboot of the two hosts?
carla_oncall: initiating drain+reboot now:```
kubectl drain node/gpu-az3-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
gcloud compute instances reset gpu-az3-07 --zone us-central1-a
```
deploy-bot: Route update applied: traffic shifted from us-central cluster -> us-east fallback for route /v1/generate (low-latency tier).
maya_platform: i'm pulling hypervisor logs and will check for PCIe AER counts from host firmware: command: `sudo lspci -vvv | grep -i aer -A3`
frank_runtime: also seeing identical PCIe vendor messages on the IOMMU side. past incidents showed this when a neighbor VM saturated PCIe bandwidth (ioctl flood).
dave_sre: good call. frank, can you dump `dmesg` from the host pre-reboot? put in the runbook link.
frank_runtime: uploaded dmesg + nvidia-smi -q for both hosts: https://internal.redwood/incident/2112345678/artifacts (contains timestamps + gzipped logs).
olivia_support: customers A,B,C affected — A had 3 failed requests, B saw 12s tail latency spikes, C observed model fallback to older variant. CS asked for ETA and blameless RCA.
carla_oncall: mitigation status: drained hosts -> rebooted -> nodes rejoined. traffic stable after route shift. CPU/GPU utilization back to baseline. still monitoring error counters.
dave_sre: hypothesis tracking: 1) Failing host DIMM -> ECC spike; 2) PCIe fabric corruption (AER) due to noisy neighbor VM; 3) GPU driver bug triggered by high kernel IRQ; 4) power/BIOS microcode regression after recent firmware push.
carla_oncall: ranking: (2) noisy neighbor and (1) DIMM most likely for now. evidence: ECC concentrated on single GPU slot, neighbor batch job started ~02:00 UTC, AER messages concurrent with heavy p2p traffic.
maya_platform: cross-checking hypervisor event logs — saw large PCIe reset events around 15:11:28 UTC on az3-07. attaching excerpt:```
2025-11-12T15:11:28Z hostd: pci_reset: device 0000:05:00.0 reset count 3
2025-11-12T15:11:29Z hostd: p2p_throttle: vm vm-internal-embeddings pid=7321 bandwidth spike
```
dave_sre: next steps: - keep drainer rule for the batch job until we repro locally - schedule health checks on remaining az3 hosts - request host vendor support for PCIe AER trace analysis - if ECC grows again, isolate and RMA GPU.
carla_oncall: i've created a follow-up ticket: INC-2112345678-RCA with initial timeline, logs, mitigation, and customer impact notes. assigning to @dave_sre for RCA writeup and to @maya_platform to coordinate vendor debug.
frank_runtime: note: driver version 525.85 was on these hosts, not the very latest. i can repro a PCIe AER + ECC increment locally with stress test container. will run overnight and post results.
olivia_support: CS will send interim customer note in 2 hours, including mitigation and ETA for RCA.
deploy-bot: Canary rollback of internal-embeddings job applied (reducing affinity to az3).
carla_oncall: handing off to daytime SREs. if anything spikes, page escalation chain. leaving channel open for RCA work. :thumbsup:
dave_sre: assigning checks to runbook: `check-pcie-aer`, `gpu-ecc-trend`, `host-firmware-compare`. will produce a 1-page RCA draft by EOD.
maya_platform: ping vendor support, attaching request id: VS-99821. asked for AER decode and PCIe lane integrity trace.
frank_runtime: saved reproduction logs and kernel oops. leaving note: to reproduce, start internal-embeddings container with `--gpus=all` and heavy p2p, monitor `nvidia-smi dmon` and `dmesg`.
olivia_support: marking incident SEV: P2 -> customer-impacting but mitigated.
carla_oncall: thanks team. closing live triage, moving to RCA thread. will update INC ticket with final timeline and link to this thread. :eyes:
